resources.string: Pierre Gallaz · developed with Claude Code
Let it cool, pull the tab of the safety valve until it hisses, then unscrew: this spares the boiler o-ring. Rinse every part and let them dry.
Filtered water, filled to the line. Never more than 8 minutes on the heat, and off the heat as soon as the espresso is out. Let the heat plate cool by itself.
A light descale: a sulfamic-acid descaler, cold, 15 minutes in the boiler. At most once a month; if it needs more, soften your water. Never lactic acid, it damages the plating.
A deep descale, with the heat exchanger submerged too — every six months where the water is hard.
With the machine apart, look at the o-rings, the valve pin and its spring: scale, grit, wear. A damaged o-ring is replaced — a spare came in the brown envelope.
